newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Assidoman to raise Sepap stake.
newsitem.headline: Assidoman to raise Sepap stake.

text.p: Swedish forestry concern Assidoman A/S said on Tuesday that it had reached an agreement with Cyprus-based holding firm Daventree to buy its 51 percent stake in Czech paper maker Sepap a.s..
"It has always been our long-term goal to increase our holdings in Sepap," said Assidoman official Lennart Ahlgren.
Details of the purchase, which will bring AssiDoman's stake in Sepap to 90 percent, were not disclosed.
Ahlgren added that AssiDoman would make a public offer for the outstanding 10 percent of Sepap, the Czech Republic's largest paper maker.

Bahamas-based investor Michael Dingman, who controls Daventree, and the Swedish forestry group came to loggerheads over Sepap when Dingman swooped onto the Czech market in October, 1995 taking a majority stake in Sepap even though AssiDoman already held 36 percent of the company.

But the two firms reached a cooperation agreement of their respective investments in Sepap in February last year only months after AssiDoman had tried in vain to place some of its representatives on the Sepap board.
